purpose: Trastuzumab-anns is used to treat certain types of breast cancer and stomach cancer that have too much of a protein called HER2 on the cancer cells. It is often used alone or combined with chemotherapy to help slow or stop cancer growth. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for your type of cancer.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have too much of a protein called HER2, which tells cancer cells to grow and multiply quickly. This medicine is like a guided missile — it attaches directly to that HER2 protein on cancer cells and blocks the signal that tells them to grow. It also helps your own immune system recognize and attack the cancer cells.
common_side_effects: Fever, chills, nausea, headache, tiredness, and diarrhea are common, especially during or after the infusion. You may also experience muscle or joint pain, infections, and low white blood cell counts. Many of these side effects are manageable, so let your care team know how you are feeling.
warnings: This medicine can sometimes cause serious heart problems, so your doctor will check your heart regularly while you are on it. It can also cause serious lung problems during or after infusions. It is not safe to use during pregnancy and can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, swelling, or a severe reaction during your infusion.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV infusion at a clinic or hospital, usually once every 1 or 3 weeks depending on your treatment plan. The first dose is given slowly over about 90 minutes, and if you tolerate it well, later doses may be given over 30 minutes. Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your weight and the type of cancer being treated.
